about: R3-EARTH-LINK EL3b.3 (design r3/earth-link.md EL3b): how Earth's feed looks at each Earth rate. The band is chosen by earth.rate (D) alone: the first band whose min <= D (and D < max, when max is given). Nothing is computed from D: the feed's speed is the sim's earth.feed frame moving with the newest light, and the band only styles it. jumble 0..1: ghosts of the weeks that flicked past; drift: a near-still frame breathes slowly; tint: the Doppler shift as a stylized warm (receding) or cool (approaching) wash, an indicator and not a spectral render (gate 2 asserts the bands at RS-26..RS-29 in tests/test_physics.gd); whirl: Earth's clock hand blurs. Calibrated on the RS values: 7.0711e-4 (top speed, astern) still, 0.070888 (0.99c astern) slow, 1 real, 14.107 (0.99c ahead) fast, 1414.2 (top speed, ahead) torrent.

sound.about: R3-EARTH-LINK EL3b.7 (Mark 2026-10-30), made exact by R3 audio realism AR8b (standing order 2026-10-30: no compromises on the physics; a True setting and labelled Processed settings). Sound from home at the comms receiver. The bed is the week's category (the sky kind plays the sky's), babble in a band whose sound is babble, static out of beam. Its time rate is the Earth rate D (earth.rate) in every setting: the bed plays at speed D and the accents come every every_s / D (the first first_s / D after the bed starts). Receiver (the default): the ship's receiver corrects the frequency, as the DSN corrects the Voyagers' Doppler shift; a real-time receiver plays between receiver.min_rate and receiver.max_rate of real time (below it holds the moment, above the backlog grows). True: speed and pitch x D, uncorrected; outside receiver.audible nothing reaches the ear and the station says so. A new bed replaces the playing one only after hold_s of the station's clock (a change of beam at once).
